entities.summary: Wilbrand of Oldenburg was a bishop of Paderborn and of Utrecht, playing a crucial role in the ecclesiastical politics of Western Europe during the 13th century. Born in the late 12th century, Wilbrand rose through the ranks to become a prominent figure in the Church, overseeing the establishment of schools and monasteries. His influence extended beyond the confines of his diocese, with him serving as a key advisor to Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II. Wilbrand's legacy, however, was not without controversy, as his efforts to consolidate power within the Church led to conflicts with other clergy and nobles. Despite this, his contributions to the development of Christian education and architecture remain an enduring testament to his impact on the region. The exact date of his birth remains unknown, but his death on August 3, 1233, marked the end of an era in the history of Western Christianity.
